text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a preterm infant with respiratory distress immediately after birth, combined with hypoxemia, mild respiratory acidosis, and a chest X-ray showing a "ground glass" appearance, is classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency.
